meta.note: Each group is the same seeds for every strategy. A strategy is judged by how often it escapes the rat race, then how fast (rolls = turns, Paydays = months); bankruptcies count against it.

policies.label: Never invests
policies.description: Pays every Doodad, passes every deal. The salary alone: what the rat race is without investing.

policies.label: Properties from cash
policies.description: Buys any property it can pay the deposit for out of cash - no loans, no reserve, small deals only.

policies.label: Picky properties
policies.description: Only properties returning at least 3% a month on the deposit, with a 2.000 reserve kept; small deals.

policies.label: Small first, Big when rich
policies.description: Draws Small Deals until cash reaches 20.000, then Big Deals; buys any property the cash pays for, keeps 1.000.

policies.label: Borrow when it pays
policies.description: Borrows the shortfall when a property pays at least 1,5 times the loan interest it adds; repays when it can.

policies.label: Leveraged, Big Deals
policies.description: Aims at Big Deals from the start and borrows whenever the property pays at least the interest.

policies.label: Marketing first, then properties
policies.description: Buys every Multi-Level-Marketing card it can afford (the best card on average), then properties from cash.

policies.label: Trade stocks for deposits
policies.description: Buys stocks at 10 or less and sells at 25 or more to raise deposit money, then buys properties.

policies.label: All-rounder
policies.description: Properties above 2% a month with a reserve, loans only when well covered, Multi-Level-Marketing, stock trading, selling to generous buyers, Big Deals once cash allows.

policies.label: Best strategy found by the search
policies.description: properties paying at least 4% a month, no reserve, borrows when the card pays for it, Big Deals from 20,000 cash, buys Multi-Level-Marketing
